dead_ends_inherited: PowerShell here-string syntax (-m @'...'@) in the BASH tool silently mangles a commit message — it commits with @ as the subject. In the Bash tool use a real heredoc; @'...'@ is PowerShell only.

py -3.11 cannot open a Git Bash /tmp/... path. curl -o /tmp/x.json actually writes to C:\Users\huida\AppData\Local\Temp\x.json. Use cygpath -w or the C:\...\Temp\ form in Python; bash tools handle /tmp fine.
Always pass an ABSOLUTE sqlite path in a Python one-liner. A relative one resolved somewhere unexpected and produced a self-contradicting read.
api_keys is the wrong table for a Hub credential — it is empty and has no hash column. Credentials live in operator_credentials; see hub/hub/db/engine.py:171 _seed_operator_credential.
py -3.11 -m openspec fails ('No module named openspec.__main__'). Use the `openspec` console script.
The PID files under ~/.agentweave/hub/ mislead. Resolve a port's real owner with `netstat -ano | grep LISTEN` then `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=N"`.
`agentweave` cannot be started from this repo's ROOT — the repo's own hub/ directory shadows the installed hub package under `python -m`. Start from hub/.
pytest hub/tests/ does NOT accept --timeout (no pytest-timeout plugin). Passing it fails the whole run with 'unrecognized arguments'.
The Bash tool's cwd PERSISTS between calls. A backgrounded `cd hub && ...` after an earlier `cd hub/ui` silently resolves wrong. Use absolute paths in backgrounded commands.
git checkout <file> to undo a scratch mutation reverts uncommitted work. Copy the file aside first.

Playwright's Python get_by_role(name=...) does not accept a callable — use re.compile(...). And page.get_by_text does not reach a rendered spec document; it renders in an iframe, so use page.frame_locator('iframe').first.

NEVER_BACKGROUND_AND_WAIT: THE BUG THAT COST RUN 2 FIFTY MINUTES. You are a `claude -p` process launched by a Scheduled Task. On 2026-08-21 three consecutive iterations (10:36, 10:52, 11:06) each started the full hub/tests/ suite in the background, wrote 'waiting for the background test run to finish', ended the turn -- and killed the suite they were waiting for. Section 6's finished work sat uncommitted across FOUR iteration boundaries until a human intervened. THE RULES: (1) Never end a turn 'waiting' for anything. There is nothing to wait for. (2) Run the full suite in the FOREGROUND if you run it. It takes ~13-16 minutes; a firing has a 2-hour execution limit, so there is plenty of room -- the 15-minute FIRING INTERVAL is not your deadline, because MultipleInstances=IgnoreNew just skips the next firing while you work. (3) If you genuinely cannot afford the full suite this turn, COMMIT AND PUSH THE WORK FIRST on the targeted tests you did run, and write 'full suite not run, next iteration must run it' into next_action. A committed section with a stated verification gap is recoverable; uncommitted work is what gets lost. (4) NEVER end an iteration with a dirty tree. That rule existed already and this is what breaking it looks like.
